A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

beta adrenergically mediated stimulation of the renin-secreteing cells of the juxtamedullary apparatus is not mediated by hemodynamics, tubular sodium reabsoption or by the renin-angiotensin feedback mechanism.
the beta adrenergically stimulated renin release is not mediated via a hemodynamic effect on the juxtaglomelular apparatus but is a direct effect of the beta receptor on the renin cell.

the renin response of the kidney to RNS is not blocked by d-propranol, but is blocked by l-propranol, indicating the presence of an intrinsic beta adrenergically mediated mechanism for renin secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta adrenergically stimulated renin response is not dependent on hemodynamic factors, and it is not dependent on tubular sodium re-absorption.
beta adrenergically mediated renin release is not a result of changes in renal hemodynamics.
the beta-adrenergic system has a major role in regulating renin secretion and that this role is independent of the effects of beta stimulation on the renal vasculature.
